title: `||` propagates NULL; `concat` and `concat_ws` skip it; `greatest`, `least` skip it
description: `'a' || NULL` is NULL, and so is `[1] || NULL`. `concat('a', NULL, 'b')` is `'ab'` and `concat(NULL, NULL)` is `''`; `concat_ws(',', 'a', NULL, 'b')` is `'a,b'`, and NULL with a NULL separator; `list_concat([1], NULL)` is `[1]`.

Other scalar functions give NULL for a NULL argument (`upper`, `length`, `substring`, `replace`), but `greatest(1, NULL, 3)` is 3 and `least(NULL, 2)` is 2: they leave NULLs out and are NULL only when every argument is.
reference: `str_concat` with `null_handling: ACCEPT_NULLS`, NULL in, NULL out; `IGNORE_NULLS` refused. sverify writes `str_concat` as DuckDB's `||`, natively.
The SQL lift reads DuckDB's `concat(…)` as `str_concat` of `coalesce(a, '')` for each argument, and `greatest`, `least` with their NULLs left out (`sql_lift/strings.py`, `sql_lift/core.py`).
